statusText: Mapped policy state: EA_ON (green). Tail 10 sits in the low band while Stress 46 remains elevated; the published danger window spans 12:30Z-15:00Z.
recommendation: The deterministic mapping holds at EA_ON because Tail remains in the low band after the post-earnings impulse was fully retraced and the marginal new overnight low at 29,401.75 was rejected rather than held. The forward path lifts Tail into the WATCH band only for the 13:00Z and 14:00Z hours covering the U.S. cash open and the first full cash hour of NVIDIA repricing, and the published danger window stays confined to 12:30Z-15:00Z rather than covering the whole session.
headline: Post-earnings gap retraced to a rejected overnight low: Tail holds at 10, Stress eases to 46 into the claims and cash-open window
body: Nasdaq-100 September futures trade at 29,446.25, up 156.75 points or 0.54%, as of 06:20Z against a previous close of 29,289.50. The defining observation of this assessment is that the post-earnings impulse has been given back rather than extended. Price reached 29,654.75 after the NVIDIA release, then retraced roughly 253 points to a marginal new overnight low of 29,401.75 and has since bounced about 45 points, so the session's most recent extreme was rejected rather than held. That is the opposite of the structure this framework treats as dangerous: there is no shallow-pullback sequence, no failed retracement followed by repeated extension, and no holding near a session extreme. A delayed second-quote source shows the same 29,401.75 low, so the reading is not an artifact of one feed. Regional cash trade tells the same story. The Nikkei 225 opened at 66,775.78, travelled a 65,782.59 to 66,954.69 band and closed at 66,091.84, down 0.26%, fading its opening gap entirely. The catalyst behind the overnight gap is verified: NVIDIA reported second-quarter fiscal 2027 revenue of 96.2 billion dollars, up 106% year on year, with data-centre revenue of 89.0 billion dollars, up 117%, GAAP earnings of 2.46 dollars per diluted share, and guided third-quarter revenue to 108.0 billion dollars plus or minus 2%. Cross-assets remain unaligned rather than stacked. VIX closed at 15.21, down 0.24 points or 1.55%, in a 15.21 to 15.74 session range. WTI is 81.33 dollars, down 1.10%, with Brent at 86.95, extending declines on reported Strait of Hormuz diplomacy, which removes rather than adds an energy amplifier even though Wednesday's Bloomberg report of a planned Russian escalation in Ukraine briefly lifted crude. Treasury yields are close to unchanged, with the 10-year at 4.655% and the 2-year at 4.22%, each up around a fifth of a basis point; the latest published H.15 daily figures are 4.64% and 4.17% for 25 August. The standing conflict is inflation: July PCE prices rose 0.2% on the month and 3.7% on the year, with core at 0.2% and 3.3%, personal income up 0.4% and spending up 0.2%. A firm yield path and an above-target headline inflation rate sitting alongside an equity market pricing an AI capital-expenditure upgrade widens the distribution of outcomes, which is a Stress condition rather than a Tail condition. Wednesday's cash session closed slightly lower, with the Nasdaq-100 index at 29,995.38, down 0.17%, so the overnight gap has still not been ratified by a cash auction. That unratified gap, not the earnings result, is why the forward path lifts Tail into the WATCH band for the two hours around the 13:30Z cash open, and the published danger window stays confined to 12:30Z-15:00Z, spanning initial jobless claims and the opening repricing. Shared Finviz cross-asset context was read but was collected at 02:15Z, roughly four hours before this assessment and beyond the 90-minute freshness threshold, so it was treated as stale and not relied upon; every level cited here comes from independent primary-source research.

lookbackSummary: Over the preceding 24 hours Claude held Tail between 10 and 16 through the Wednesday European and U.S. sessions, with Stress climbing from 52 to 61 as the market positioned into July PCE and the NVIDIA print. Tail stepped to 21 for the 20:00Z hour containing the earnings release, then decayed through 18, 16, 13, 12, 11 and 10 as the reaction proved two-sided rather than one-way. The two hourly slots at 21:00Z on 26 August and 00:00Z on 27 August have no published Claude assessment and are marked unavailable.
outlookSummary: The forward window holds Tail between 10 and 11 across the remaining Asian and European hours on the observation that the post-earnings spike has already been retraced and the most recent overnight low was rejected rather than held. It rises to 15 for the hour containing initial jobless claims at 12:30Z and to 20 for the cash-open hour and the first full cash hour, the only stretch mapped to WATCH, then decays back toward 10 through the U.S. afternoon and the overnight session, with a small lift into the Friday European pre-open ahead of the Jackson Hole keynote. The published danger window is confined to 12:30Z-15:00Z. Every forecast value beyond the current clock-hour is conditional risk rather than observed structure, and the escalation conditions named in each hour are shallow or absent pullbacks, repeated extension after a failed retracement, and NQ holding near a session extreme.
